title: Arpeggios and chord tones
description: Memorize chord-tone roles, common seventh-chord tones, and how to connect arpeggios at the change.

cards.front: What is an arpeggio in lead playing, and what does outlining the changes mean?
cards.back: An arpeggio is a chord played one note at a time. Outlining the changes means playing each chord’s tones as the harmony passes, so the listener hears the chords inside the melody even without a rhythm guitar.
Arriving on a chosen chord tone at a chord change, often the third or seventh, so the line points clearly at the harmony.

cards.front: Which chord tones carry quality, and what do root and fifth do?
cards.back: The third and seventh decide the quality, so landing on them states the chord most clearly. The root restates the center; the fifth adds stability.

cards.front: Where should chord tones go for clear outlining?
cards.back: On strong beats. A non-chord note on a strong beat creates tension, which is a different effect. Let other notes lead into the chord tones.

cards.front: Spell the tones of Dm7, G7, Cmaj7, A7, D7, and E7.
cards.back: Dm7 D F A C; G7 G B D F; Cmaj7 C E G B; A7 A C♯ E G; D7 D F♯ A C; E7 E G♯ B D.

cards.front: At a chord change, how do you connect arpeggios?
cards.back: Find the closest chord tone of the new chord to where the line currently ends. The best connection is usually one fret or one scale step.

cards.front: In a ii V I, which Dm7 tones already sit next to G7?
cards.back: The seventh of Dm7 (C) is a half step above B, the third of G7. The third of Dm7 (F) is the seventh of G7.
No. Each is a subset of the scale pattern you are already in: the tones of a seventh chord are every other note of its scale.

cards.front: On strings 2 and 1, what one-bar Dm7 outline uses D F A C, and what are the roles?
Continue that C-major line: G7 notes B G F D, then the Cmaj7 target.
cards.back: G7: 1/7, 1/3, 2/6, 2/3 (3rd, root, 7th, 5th). Cmaj7 target: E at 2/5 (3rd).

cards.front: In that top-two-string ii V I, what are the two targeting moves?
cards.back: Last Dm7 note C (1/8) steps down a half step to B (1/7), the third of G7. The G7 line ends on D (2/3), which steps up a whole step to E (2/5), the third of Cmaj7.

cards.front: Over A7 to D7, which one-fret move targets the new third on string 1?
cards.back: End the A7 idea on G (the seventh, fret 3) and step to F♯ (the third of D7, fret 2).

cards.front: From D7 to E7 on string 1, what one-fret move targets the new third?
cards.back: End the D7 idea on A (its fifth, fret 5) and step down a half step to G♯ (the third of E7, fret 4). Same idea: one fret toward the new chord’s third.

cards.front: What is the four-step practice order for arpeggios through changes?
cards.back: One chord, ascending and descending in one position. Two chords, connecting closest tones. A whole progression, one chord per bar, steady pulse. Then rest between arpeggios and play each as a phrase.

cards.front: For Am7 D7 Gmaj7, name a one-fret or one-step connection at each change.
cards.back: Am7’s seventh G sits a half step above F♯, the third of D7. D7’s seventh C then steps down to B, the third of Gmaj7.
